24	
25	metadata = MetaData()
26	
27	offices = Table(
28	    "offices",
29	    metadata,
30	    Column("id", Integer, primary_key=True),
31	    Column("name", String, nullable=False, unique=True),
32	)
33	
34	people = Table(
35	    "people",
36	    metadata,
37	    Column("id", Integer, primary_key=True),
38	    Column("email", String, nullable=False, unique=True),
39	    Column("name", String, nullable=False),
40	    Column("home_office_id", Integer, ForeignKey("offices.id"), nullable=False),
41	    Column("is_office_manager", Boolean, nullable=False, default=False),
42	    Column("active", Boolean, nullable=False, default=True),
43	)
44	
45	_person_columns = (
46	    people.c.id,
47	    people.c.email,
48	    people.c.name,
49	    people.c.home_office_id,
50	    offices.c.name.label("home_office_name"),
51	    people.c.is_office_manager,
52	    people.c.active,
53	)
54	
55	
56	def _person_select():
57	    return select(*_person_columns).join(offices, people.c.home_office_id == offices.c.id)
58	
59	
60	def search_active(session: Session, text: str, limit: int) -> Sequence[Row]:
61	    """Active people whose name contains `text`, ignoring case, sorted by name.
62	
63	    Matched and sorted in Python with `casefold()`, because SQLite's `lower()` folds
64	    only ASCII (a few hundred rows, so this is cheap).
65	    """
66	    needle = text.casefold()
67	    rows = session.execute(_person_select().where(people.c.active.is_(True))).all()
68	    matches = [row for row in rows if needle in row.name.casefold()]
69	    matches.sort(key=lambda row: (row.name.casefold(), row.id))
70	    return matches[:limit]
71	
72	
73	def get_person(session: Session, person_id: int) -> Row | None:
74	    return session.execute(_person_select().where(people.c.id == person_id)).first()

81	class PersonRecord:
82	    email: str
83	    name: str
84	    office: str
85	    is_office_manager: bool

92	    added: int

98	def ensure_offices(session: Session, names: Iterable[str]) -> tuple[dict[str, int], int]:
99	    """Create any missing offices by name. Returns name -> id and how many were created."""
100	    existing = {name: id_ for id_, name in session.execute(select(offices.c.id, offices.c.name))}
101	    created = 0
102	    for name in sorted(set(names) - existing.keys()):
103	        existing[name] = session.execute(insert(offices).values(name=name)).inserted_primary_key[0]
104	        created += 1
105	    return existing, created
106	
107	
108	def load_people(session: Session, records: Sequence[PersonRecord]) -> LoadResult:
109	    """Upsert people keyed on email; mark anyone missing inactive. Never deletes."""
110	    office_ids, offices_created = ensure_offices(session, (r.office for r in records))

"""Tables and queries for `offices` and `people`.

Imported only by `people.service` and the seed CLI (AD-1). The tables are created
by Alembic (AD-10); these definitions describe them for queries.
"""

from collections.abc import Iterable, Sequence
from dataclasses import dataclass

from sqlalchemy import (
    Boolean,
    Column,
    ForeignKey,
    Integer,
    MetaData,
    Row,
    String,
    Table,
    insert,
    select,
    update,
)
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

metadata = MetaData()

offices = Table(
    "offices",
    metadata,
    Column("id", Integer, primary_key=True),
    Column("name", String, nullable=False, unique=True),
)

people = Table(
    "people",
    metadata,
    Column("id", Integer, primary_key=True),
    Column("email", String, nullable=False, unique=True),
    Column("name", String, nullable=False),
    Column("home_office_id", Integer, ForeignKey("offices.id"), nullable=False),
    Column("is_office_manager", Boolean, nullable=False, default=False),
    Column("active", Boolean, nullable=False, default=True),
)

_person_columns = (
    people.c.id,
    people.c.email,
    people.c.name,
    people.c.home_office_id,
    offices.c.name.label("home_office_name"),
    people.c.is_office_manager,
    people.c.active,
)


def _person_select():
    return select(*_person_columns).join(offices, people.c.home_office_id == offices.c.id)


def search_active(session: Session, text: str, limit: int) -> Sequence[Row]:
    """Active people whose name contains `text`, ignoring case, sorted by name.

    Matched and sorted in Python with `casefold()`, because SQLite's `lower()` folds
    only ASCII (a few hundred rows, so this is cheap).
    """
    needle = text.casefold()
    rows = session.execute(_person_select().where(people.c.active.is_(True))).all()
    matches = [row for row in rows if needle in row.name.casefold()]
    matches.sort(key=lambda row: (row.name.casefold(), row.id))
    return matches[:limit]


def get_person(session: Session, person_id: int) -> Row | None:
    return session.execute(_person_select().where(people.c.id == person_id)).first()


# --- writes, used only by the seed CLI (AD-3, AD-9) ---------------------------


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PersonRecord:
    email: str
    name: str
    office: str
    is_office_manager: bool


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class LoadResult:
    offices_created: int
    offices_total: int
    added: int
    updated: int
    reactivated: int
    deactivated_ids: tuple[int, ...]


def ensure_offices(session: Session, names: Iterable[str]) -> tuple[dict[str, int], int]:
    """Create any missing offices by name. Returns name -> id and how many were created."""
    existing = {name: id_ for id_, name in session.execute(select(offices.c.id, offices.c.name))}
    created = 0
    for name in sorted(set(names) - existing.keys()):
        existing[name] = session.execute(insert(offices).values(name=name)).inserted_primary_key[0]
        created += 1
    return existing, created


def load_people(session: Session, records: Sequence[PersonRecord]) -> LoadResult:
    """Upsert people keyed on email; mark anyone missing inactive. Never deletes."""
    office_ids, offices_created = ensure_offices(session, (r.office for r in records))
    current = {
        row.email: row
        for row in session.execute(select(people.c.id, people.c.email, people.c.active))
    }
    added = updated = reactivated = 0
    for record in records:
        values = {
            "name": record.name,
            "home_office_id": office_ids[record.office],
            "is_office_manager": record.is_office_manager,
            "active": True,
        }
        row = current.get(record.email)
        if row is None:
            session.execute(insert(people).values(email=record.email, **values))
            added += 1
        else:
            session.execute(update(people).where(people.c.id == row.id).values(**values))
            updated += 1
            if not row.active:
                reactivated += 1

    seen = {r.email for r in records}
    deactivated = tuple(
        sorted(row.id for email, row in current.items() if row.active and email not in seen)
    )
    if deactivated:
        session.execute(update(people).where(people.c.id.in_(deactivated)).values(active=False))

    return LoadResult(
        offices_created=offices_created,
        offices_total=len(office_ids),
        added=added,
        updated=updated,
        reactivated=reactivated,
        deactivated_ids=deactivated,
    )

"""Application factory: routes, static files, templates, the identity redirect and the
domain error handler."""

import logging
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.staticfiles import StaticFiles
from fastapi.templating import Jinja2Templates

from roombooker.core.errors import DomainError, domain_error_handler
from roombooker.core.identity import NeedsPerson, needs_person_handler, path_with_query, pick_url
from roombooker.people import web as people_web
from roombooker.people.service import can_manage_office
from roombooker.rooms import web as rooms_web

PACKAGE_DIR = Path(__file__).parent


def _configure_logging() -> None:
    logger = logging.getLogger("roombooker")
    logger.setLevel(logging.INFO)
    if not logger.handlers:
        handler = logging.StreamHandler(sys.stdout)
        handler.setFormatter(logging.Formatter("%(levelname)s %(name)s: %(message)s"))
        logger.addHandler(handler)


def create_app() -> FastAPI:
    _configure_logging()
    app = FastAPI(title="Room Booking", docs_url=None, redoc_url=None, openapi_url=None)

    templates = Jinja2Templates(directory=PACKAGE_DIR / "templates")
    templates.env.globals["pick_url"] = pick_url
    templates.env.globals["path_with_query"] = path_with_query
    templates.env.globals["can_manage_office"] = can_manage_office
    app.state.templates = templates

    app.mount("/static", StaticFiles(directory=PACKAGE_DIR / "static"), name="static")
    app.add_exception_handler(NeedsPerson, needs_person_handler)
    app.add_exception_handler(DomainError, domain_error_handler)
    app.include_router(people_web.router)
    app.include_router(rooms_web.router)
    return app


app = create_app()

2	
3	The only writer of `rooms` (AD-3). Every function takes the acting person and
4	raises `NotAllowed` unless they manage the room's office (AD-7, RULE-4).
5	"""
6	
7	import logging
8	from collections.abc import Callable
9	from dataclasses import dataclass
10	
11	from sqlalchemy import Row
12	from sqlalchemy.exc import IntegrityError
13	from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
14	
15	from roombooker.core.errors import DomainError, NotAllowed
16	from roombooker.people.service import Person, can_manage_office
17	from roombooker.rooms import store
18	
19	log = logging.getLogger("roombooker.rooms")
20	
21	NAME_MAX_LENGTH = 50
22	CAPACITY_MIN = 1
23	CAPACITY_MAX = 200
24	SQLITE_MAX_INTEGER = 2**63 - 1
25	
26	NEEDS_NAME = "Give the room a name."
27	NAME_TOO_LONG = f"Room names can be up to {NAME_MAX_LENGTH} characters."
28	BAD_CAPACITY = f"Capacity must be a whole number from {CAPACITY_MIN} to {CAPACITY_MAX}."
29	
30	
31	@dataclass(frozen=True)
32	class Room:
33	    id: int
34	    office_id: int
35	    name: str
36	    capacity: int
37	    is_closed: bool
38	
39	    @property
40	    def status(self) -> str:
41	        return "Closed" if self.is_closed else "Open"
42	
43	
44	class RoomNotFound(DomainError):
45	    status_code = 404
46	    default_message = "That room does not exist."
47	
48	
49	class InvalidRoom(DomainError):
50	    """The submitted name or capacity breaks a rule. Carries every reason and the typed values."""
51	
52	    status_code = 422
53	
54	    def __init__(self, errors: list[str], values: dict[str, str]):
55	        super().__init__(" ".join(errors))
56	        self.errors = errors
57	        self.values = values
58	
59	
60	def _to_room(row: Row) -> Room:
61	    return Room(
62	        id=row.id,
63	        office_id=row.office_id,
64	        name=row.name,
65	        capacity=row.capacity,
66	        is_closed=row.is_closed,
67	    )
68	
69	
70	def _name_key(name: str) -> str:
71	    """Duplicate check key: SQLite's lower() folds only ASCII, so compare in Python."""
72	    return name.strip().casefold()
73	
74	
75	def _require_manager(actor: Person, office_id: int, action: str) -> None:
76	    if not can_manage_office(actor, office_id):
77	        log.info("rooms: person_id=%d refused %s for office_id=%d", actor.id, action, office_id)
78	        raise NotAllowed()
79	
80	
81	def _get_row(session: Session, room_id: int) -> Row:
82	    # Ids outside SQLite's INTEGER range cannot exist (and would fail to bind).
83	    row = store.get(session, room_id) if 0 < room_id <= SQLITE_MAX_INTEGER else None
84	    if row is None:
85	        raise RoomNotFound()
86	    return row
87	
88	
89	def _duplicate_of(
90	    session: Session, office_id: int, name: str, room_id: int | None
91	) -> Row | None:
92	    """Another room in the office with this name, ignoring case and surrounding spaces."""
93	    key = _name_key(name)

101	    session: Session, actor: Person, name: str, capacity: str, room_id: int | None
102	) -> tuple[str, int]:
103	    """Trimmed name and whole-number capacity, or InvalidRoom with every reason."""
104	    values = {"name": name, "capacity": capacity}
105	    errors: list[str] = []
106	
107	    clean_name = name.strip()
108	    if not clean_name:
109	        errors.append(NEEDS_NAME)
110	    elif len(clean_name) > NAME_MAX_LENGTH:
111	        errors.append(NAME_TOO_LONG)
112	    else:
113	        duplicate = _duplicate_of(session, actor.home_office_id, clean_name, room_id)
114	        if duplicate is not None:
115	            errors.append(_duplicate_reason(actor, duplicate.name))
116	
117	    raw_capacity = capacity.strip()
118	    clean_capacity = None
119	    if raw_capacity.isascii() and raw_capacity.isdigit() and len(raw_capacity) <= 4:
120	        clean_capacity = int(raw_capacity)
121	    if clean_capacity is None or not CAPACITY_MIN <= clean_capacity <= CAPACITY_MAX:
122	        errors.append(BAD_CAPACITY)
123	
124	    if errors:
125	        raise InvalidRoom(errors, values)
126	    return clean_name, clean_capacity

130	    return f"{actor.home_office_name} already has a room called {existing_name}."

133	def _commit_details[T](
134	    session: Session, actor: Person, name: str, capacity: str, write: Callable[[], T]
135	) -> T:
136	    """Run `write` and commit, mapping the exact-match unique constraint (a backstop
137	    behind the case-insensitive check) to InvalidRoom."""
138	    try:
139	        result = write()
140	        session.commit()
141	        return result
142	    except IntegrityError:
143	        session.rollback()
144	        raise InvalidRoom(
145	            [_duplicate_reason(actor, name.strip())], {"name": name, "capacity": capacity}
146	        ) from None

149	def list_rooms(session: Session, actor: Person) -> list[Room]:
150	    """The actor's home-office rooms, sorted by name."""
151	    _require_manager(actor, actor.home_office_id, "list")
152	    rooms = [_to_room(row) for row in store.list_for_office(session, actor.home_office_id)]
153	    rooms.sort(key=lambda room: (room.name.casefold(), room.id))
154	    return rooms

165	    """Create an Open room in the actor's home office."""

167	    clean_name, clean_capacity = _validate(session, actor, name, capacity, room_id=None)
168	    room_id = _commit_details(
169	        session,
170	        actor,
171	        name,
172	        capacity,
173	        lambda: store.insert(session, actor.home_office_id, clean_name, clean_capacity),
174	    )
175	    log.info("rooms: person_id=%d add room_id=%d", actor.id, room_id)
176	    return Room(room_id, actor.home_office_id, clean_name, clean_capacity, is_closed=False)

180	    """Change a room's name and capacity. Its status is unchanged."""
181	    row = _get_row(session, room_id)

183	    clean_name, clean_capacity = _validate(session, actor, name, capacity, room_id=room_id)

187	        name,

190	    )

192	    return Room(room_id, row.office_id, clean_name, clean_capacity, row.is_closed)
193	
194	
195	def _set_closed(session: Session, actor: Person, room_id: int, is_closed: bool) -> Room:
196	    action = "close" if is_closed else "reopen"
197	    row = _get_row(session, room_id)
198	    _require_manager(actor, row.office_id, action)
199	    store.set_closed(session, room_id, is_closed)
200	    session.commit()
201	    log.info("rooms: person_id=%d %s room_id=%d", actor.id, action, room_id)
202	    return Room(row.id, row.office_id, row.name, row.capacity, is_closed)

204

206	    return _set_closed(session, actor, room_id, is_closed=True)
207	
208	
209	def reopen_room(session: Session, actor: Person, room_id: int) -> Room:
210	    return _set_closed(session, actor, room_id, is_closed=False)

"""Table and queries for `rooms`.

Imported only by `rooms.service` (AD-1, AD-3). The table is created by Alembic
(AD-10); this definition describes it for queries.
"""

from collections.abc import Sequence

from sqlalchemy import Boolean, Column, Integer, MetaData, Row, String, Table, select, update
from sqlalchemy import insert as sa_insert
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

metadata = MetaData()

rooms = Table(
    "rooms",
    metadata,
    Column("id", Integer, primary_key=True),
    Column("office_id", Integer, nullable=False),  # FK to offices.id in the database
    Column("name", String, nullable=False),
    Column("capacity", Integer, nullable=False),
    Column("is_closed", Boolean, nullable=False, default=False),
)


def list_for_office(session: Session, office_id: int) -> Sequence[Row]:
    return session.execute(select(rooms).where(rooms.c.office_id == office_id)).all()


def get(session: Session, room_id: int) -> Row | None:
    return session.execute(select(rooms).where(rooms.c.id == room_id)).first()


def insert(session: Session, office_id: int, name: str, capacity: int) -> int:
    result = session.execute(
        sa_insert(rooms).values(office_id=office_id, name=name, capacity=capacity, is_closed=False)
    )
    return result.inserted_primary_key[0]


def update_details(session: Session, room_id: int, name: str, capacity: int) -> None:
    session.execute(update(rooms).where(rooms.c.id == room_id).values(name=name, capacity=capacity))


def set_closed(session: Session, room_id: int, is_closed: bool) -> None:
    session.execute(update(rooms).where(rooms.c.id == room_id).values(is_closed=is_closed))

"""Shared fixtures: a temporary SQLite file migrated to head through Alembic."""

import sqlite3
from pathlib import Path

import pytest
from alembic import command
from alembic.config import Config
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from roombooker import seed
from roombooker.app import create_app
from roombooker.core import db

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
CSV_HEADER = "email,name,office,office_manager"


def migrate_to_head() -> None:
    config = Config(str(ROOT / "alembic.ini"))
    config.attributes["configure_logger"] = False  # keep pytest's log capture intact
    command.upgrade(config, "head")


@pytest.fixture
def db_path(tmp_path, monkeypatch) -> Path:
    path = tmp_path / "var" / "roombooker.db"
    monkeypatch.setenv("ROOMBOOKER_DB_PATH", str(path))
    monkeypatch.delenv("ROOMBOOKER_ENV", raising=False)
    migrate_to_head()
    yield path
    db.get_engine().dispose()
    db._engine_for.cache_clear()


@pytest.fixture
def load_csv(db_path, tmp_path):
    """Write CSV lines (after the header) to a file and run the seed CLI on it."""
    counter = iter(range(1, 1_000))

    def _load(*lines: str, header: str = CSV_HEADER) -> int:
        path = tmp_path / f"people-{next(counter)}.csv"
        path.write_text("\n".join([header, *lines]) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
        return seed.main([str(path)])

    return _load


@pytest.fixture
def people(db_path):
    """Read the people table as {email: row dict}, straight from the file."""

    def _people() -> dict[str, dict]:
        with sqlite3.connect(db_path) as conn:
            conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
            rows = conn.execute(
                "SELECT p.id, p.email, p.name, o.name AS office, p.is_office_manager, p.active "
                "FROM people p JOIN offices o ON o.id = p.home_office_id"
            ).fetchall()
        return {row["email"]: dict(row) for row in rows}

    return _people


@pytest.fixture
def client(db_path) -> TestClient:
    with TestClient(create_app(), follow_redirects=False) as test_client:
        yield test_client

Base directory for this skill: /home/claude/runs/room-booker/.claude/skills/bmad-review

# BMad Review

Review content through lenses — each a distinct method and stance — and report findings in one canonical shape. Report what is real — never pad to look thorough. Each lens sets its own stance toward the content and toward zero findings: for most an empty result is valid; the adversarial lens requires at least ten concrete findings and treats an empty list as a signal to re-check; the editorial lenses hold content sacrosanct and critique only how it is organized and expressed.

The lens set is whatever `{workflow.lenses}` resolves to, not a fixed list — overrides add lenses and replace shipped ones. Never claim a capability from this file; read the resolved lenses and work from those.

## Inputs

- **content** — what to review: a diff, branch, uncommitted changes, file, ticket (initiative, epic, story, spike, bug), or any document. Args: `[path]`.
- **lenses** (optional) — one or more lens codes or names, however the caller expresses them: a spoken request, or a directive of the form `skill:bmad-review lenses=<code>[,<code>...]` (the form bmm's `doc_standards` uses). Default: every applicable lens (a full review).
- **also_consider** (optional) — areas to keep in mind alongside each lens's normal analysis.
- **claims** (optional) — the change's own narrative: the commit messages it covers, or whatever description of it the caller supplied. Goes to the edge-case lens alone.
- **pre-resolved customization** (optional) — `[workflow]` field values supplied by a forwarding caller. See Execution step 1.

## Conventions

- Bare paths (e.g. `references/lens-edge-case-hunter.md`) resolve from `{skill-root}` — this skill's installed directory, where `customize.toml` lives. `{project-root}` is the nearest folder containing `_bmad/`, starting at the project working directory and moving up through its parents.
- `{workflow.<name>}` resolves to fields in `customize.toml`'s `[workflow]` table (overrides win per BMad merge rules).
- In `style_guide`, `review_guidance`, and `persistent_facts`, a value prefixed `file:` is a path or glob — load that file's contents. If a `file:` value cannot be read, name the failed file in the output header and continue: the shipped baseline for `style_guide`, the remaining entries otherwise.

## Execution

1. **Resolve customization:** `uv run {project-root}/_bmad/scripts/resolve_customization.py --skill {skill-root} --project-root {project-root} --key workflow`.
   - Script not found: BMad is not set up here. Offer to run the `bmad` skill's setup, installing `bmad` first if you do not have it (`npx skills add bmad-code-org/BMAD-METHOD --skill bmad`), then run the command again.
   - Any other failure: read `{skill-root}/customize.toml` directly and use defaults.

   **Forwarded activation:** if a caller invoked you with pre-resolved customization fields (e.g. the `bmad-editorial-review` shim), honor them verbatim for those named fields — they already carry the user's overrides — and resolve only the remaining fields from your own `customize.toml`. Then execute each `{workflow.activation_steps_prepend}` entry in order, hold `{workflow.persistent_facts}` as standing context for the session, and treat `{workflow.review_guidance}` entries as standing review directives for every lens.
2. **Load the content.** Stage it once as a file: when the content is a branch, uncommitted work, or a commit range, use the repository's version-control tooling to write the unified diff to a uniquely-named file in the system temp directory and take that file's absolute path as the content. A branch means its diff against the merge base with its base branch; uncommitted work includes untracked files. Stage `claims` to its own file the same way — it is input for one lens, staged separately precisely so the other lenses never see it. If the user or caller named lenses, run exactly those only — `applies_to` and `when` do not filter an explicit request. - `lens` — the code of the lens that produced it

- `trigger_condition` — the problem, or the condition that exposes it, in one line

content.content:
# Adversarial Lens

Conduct a review of the provided content.
Look for what's missing, not only what's wrong.
Find at least ten issues to fix or improve.
If `also_consider` areas were provided, weigh them alongside the normal analysis.
If the content is empty, stop and say so.
If you have zero findings, re-check and keep thinking; do not stop with an empty list.

## Findings shape

Emit each finding with the canonical fields:

- `location` — where in the content (file:line for code, section or heading for documents, "general" when it spans the whole artifact)
- `trigger_condition` — the problem, in one line
- `guard_snippet` — the concrete fix or improvement
- `potential_consequence` — what goes wrong if it ships unaddressed

No severity, priority, or ranking.
# Edge-Case Lens

You are a pure path tracer. Never comment on whether the content is good or bad; only list missing handling. Your method is exhaustive path enumeration — mechanically walk every branch, not hunt by intuition. Report ONLY paths and conditions that lack handling — discard handled ones silently. Do not editorialize or add filler.

**MANDATORY: Execute the steps below IN EXACT ORDER. DO NOT skip steps or change the sequence. Each action within a step is a REQUIRED action to complete that step.**

**Scope rules:**

- When the content is a diff, scan only the diff hunks and list boundaries that are directly reachable from the changed lines and lack an explicit guard in the diff.
- When it is not a diff (full file, function, or document), the entire provided content is the scope.
- Ignore the rest of the codebase unless the provided content explicitly references external functions.
- When the launch message names a claims file, do NOT read it before Step 4: the path tracing in Steps 1–2 must finish before the narrative is seen.

## Step 1: Exhaustive path analysis

Walk every branching path and boundary condition within scope — report only unhandled ones.

- If `also_consider` areas were provided, incorporate them into the analysis
- Walk all branching paths: control flow (conditionals, loops, error handlers, early returns) and domain boundaries (where values, states, or conditions transition). Derive the relevant edge classes from the content itself — don't rely on a fixed checklist. Examples: missing else/default, unguarded inputs, off-by-one loops, arithmetic overflow, implicit type coercion, race conditions, timeout gaps
- Consider implicit branches: the diff special-cases or changes the handling of one or more members of a fixed set of values — enums, status codes, sentinels, type tags, flags, value ranges. The rest of the set is implicit branches (e.g. the diff changes the `RED` and `YELLOW` cases of a `RED`/`YELLOW`/`GREEN` enum; `GREEN` is the implicit branch)
- Consider handle lifetime: when the changed code re-checks, re-fetches, or re-validates something it already held — a handle, index, id, pointer — the re-check exists because an intervening call can invalidate it. Identify that call, what it does to the thing held, and what the changed code silently skips when the re-check fails
- For each call site the diff adds or changes — in test files as well as production code — read the callee's declaration and check the call against it: argument count, order, types, and defaults. Report any mismatch
- For each path: determine whether the content handles it
- Collect only the unhandled paths as findings — discard handled ones silently

## Step 2: Validate completeness

- Revisit every edge class from Step 1 — e.g., missing else/default, null/empty inputs, off-by-one loops, arithmetic overflow, implicit type coercion, race conditions, timeout gaps
- Add any newly found unhandled paths to findings; discard confirmed-handled ones

## Step 3: Deletion check

Runs only when the diff removed or replaced meaningful code (ignore pure renames and whitespace). Subordinate to the edge-case pass; findings are usually few or none.

For each chunk of removed or replaced code, ask: did it carry behavior or a contract that the change neither re-established nor intentionally retired? Add a finding for any resulting regression, orphaned reference, or newly-dead code. Skip anything already covered by your edge-case findings. Add nothing if nothing qualifies.

Deletion findings go in the same array with the four standard fields plus:

- `kind`: `"deletion"`
- `confidence`: `"high"`, `"medium"`, or `"low"` — these are inferences; rate them

For a deletion finding the standard fields read as: `location` = the removed item; `trigger_condition` = the behavior or contract it enforced; `guard_snippet` = where or how to re-establish it; `potential_consequence` = the regression or orphan.

## Step 4: Claims check

Runs only when the message that launched you named a claims file. Read that file now, for the first time; the path tracing is finished and the claims cannot steer it retroactively.

The file holds the change's own narrative — commit messages and any stated description. The narrative is the author's testimony, not evidence: a claim repeated in a code comment is still the same claim, not confirmation. Extract each checkable claim — what the change does, what it preserves, ordering, arithmetic, and parity with existing code ("exactly as X does") — then try to falsify each one against the code you have already traced. Where your trace is not enough to decide, read the code that decides it: the compared-to function, the actual callee, the state the claim assumes.

Claim findings go in the same array with the four standard fields plus:

- `kind`: `"claim"`
- `confidence`: `"high"`, `"medium"`, or `"low"`

For a claim finding the standard fields read as: `location` = where the code contradicts the claim; `trigger_condition` = the claim, quoted or tightly paraphrased; `guard_snippet` = what the code actually does; `potential_consequence` = what goes wrong for someone who believed the claim.

Verified claims produce nothing. Add nothing if nothing is falsified.

## Findings shape

Each edge-case finding contains exactly these four fields:

```json
[{
  "location": "file:start-end (or file:line when single line, or file:hunk when exact line unavailable)",
  "trigger_condition": "one-line description (max 15 words)",
  "guard_snippet": "minimal code sketch that closes the gap (single-line escaped string, no raw newlines or unescaped quotes)",
  "potential_consequence": "what could actually go wrong (max 15 words)"
}]
```

An empty array is valid when nothing is found. Do not assign severity labels, rankings, or priority levels.
# Verification-Gap Lens

**Goal:** Find behavior this change altered that could break later without any test failing. Do not hunt for bugs; report the ones you run into while tracing.

A gap finding is a request to add or change one test. File it only when you can name a specific regression that test would catch. If no such test is worth writing, there is nothing to file.

Gap shapes:

1. **Regression gap:** the changed code could regress where it is used, and no test would fail.
2. **Missing-adoption gap:** a site that should use the new behavior still handles the case its own way, and no test would catch that.
3. **Broken-verification gap:** a test looks like it covers the change but does not: it is skipped, flaky, not run normally, or too weak to see the regression.
4. **Stale-verification gap:** a test this change made wrong or moot. It may still pass.

## Evidence rules

- Read a test before saying what it covers or misses.
- Before saying no test exists, search the repo for the symbol under test and its imports. Expected file locations are not enough.
- Say what you checked and how far you looked. Drop any finding you cannot ground.
- Do not assign severity, confidence, priority, or ranking.

## Sequence

### Step 1: Screen

Take each part of the change separately. Skip a part that changes no behavior: no change to return values, thrown errors, side effects callers can see, or observable state (including iteration order and emitted messages). Formatting, comments, renames, trivial getters and pass-throughs, and type-only changes are examples. Once a part is skipped, do not look at its callers or tests.

Also skip parts that are not worth a test: static text such as prompts, skills, and documents; LLM output; and build, toolchain, dependency, and configuration changes that the build or CI run itself checks. Deterministic code that builds a prompt or request, or handles a model's response, is still eligible; the model call itself is not, and existing tests that call a model are not precedent for more.

Do not skip test-only parts. A deleted or weakened test is checked in Step 4; every touched test is read in Step 5.

If every part is skipped, return zero findings (`[]`). When the output format includes a markdown report, note there that the change is non-behavioral; a caller's exact zero-findings output contract wins over this note.

### Step 2: Name the changed behavior

For each remaining part, say what behavior differs from before: output, side effect, branch, error path, schema or event shape, default, validation rule, external contract. Handle each behavior separately.

### Step 3: Find where it is used

Trace each changed behavior to the code that observes it: direct callers, registered entry points (routes, commands, DI), and contract consumers (schemas, events, APIs, database readers).

Stop a path when a test there would catch a regression, when the consumer does not observe the change, or when the next hop is a guess (dynamic dispatch, reflection, code outside the repo). One to three hops is usually enough. With more than five similar consumers, check representative ones and expand only when a consumer uses the behavior differently.

### Step 4: Name the regression, then check the test

For each consumer, name the smallest realistic regression it would see: the branch inverted, the default dropped, the field omitted, the old error code returned, the integration call skipped. This is the Demonstration. It describes what goes wrong for the consumer. "This line could be removed without a test failing" is not a regression. If there is no regression (the state is unreachable, the branch is defensive, the code repeats what another line already guarantees), drop the path. There is no finding and nowhere else to file it.

A missing-adoption gap needs two things: evidence the change means the new behavior to replace the local one (PR intent, naming or docs, a replaced sibling site, deleted duplicate logic, a test defining the new rule), and the same observable contract at both sites. Without both, it is a refactor suggestion, not a finding. With both, missing coverage of the non-adoption is the gap.

Read the relevant test. Would the Demonstration make an assertion fail?

- Yes: the behavior is verified. No finding.
- No test runs the path, or the test is skipped, flaky, or not run normally, or it runs the code without checking the changed result: report a regression gap or broken-verification gap.
- No test asserts the site adopts the new behavior: report a missing-adoption gap.

A test counts only when it runs normally and an assertion observes the changed output, branch, or contract. These do not count: assertions on source text; success, no-throw, or snapshot-only checks; mock or log-call checks; manual checks; tests that mock away the integration; end-to-end tests that pass through without checking the changed output; stale assertions or fixtures. For example, `expect(x ?? DEFAULT).toBe(DEFAULT)` passes when `x` is missing.

Common patterns: a helper test covers the branch but caller values skip it; a payload or schema change is not checked at the consumer; migration tests only create new-format rows; a handled partial-failure path has no test; a deleted or weakened test leaves behavior unpinned (deleting a source-text assertion is not this).

### Step 5: Check the touched tests

A test is wrong when what it asserts is not what the code should do after this change. A test or test comment is moot when it no longer exercises or describes anything. Report either as a stale-verification gap, saying what the test should assert instead, or that it should go.

### Step 6: Confirm

Before writing a finding, re-open the tests or search results it relies on. Check that the Demonstration names a regression and no test you read would catch it, or that the stale assertion pins the outcome you say it does. Explain why the test misses the regression from what it sets up and checks.

Do not report: cases the compiler or type checker enforces; behavior an integration, contract, or end-to-end test already verifies; low coverage or a missing test file by itself; untested code the change did not touch.

Defects you ran into while tracing are reported with `gap_shape: "other"`. Do not go looking for more.

## Findings shape

Emit each gap with the canonical fields plus this lens's extras:

- `location` — the behavior or contract that changed, `file:line`
- `trigger_condition` — the gap, in one line
- `guard_snippet` — the test to add or change: the assertion or check that is absent, or how the stale assertion should read, fit to how this repo already tests
- `potential_consequence` — the regression, and why the tests you read would not fail; for a missing-adoption gap, the case the site mishandles; for a stale-verification gap, what the code should do, and why the test does not say so
- `gap_shape` — `"regression-gap"`, `"missing-adoption-gap"`, `"broken-verification-gap"`, `"stale-verification-gap"`, or `"other"`
- `consumer` — the impacted consumer or site, named concretely with `file:line`, not "callers of this function"
- `evidence` — what the relevant test asserts, with `file:line`; or the searches run and their result; for a broken-verification gap, why the apparent test does not count; for a stale-verification gap, the assertion that is wrong or moot

For `gap_shape: "other"` findings the four canonical fields suffice (description only); `consumer` and `evidence` are optional. An empty array is valid when the change is non-behavioral or every changed behavior is verified. When this lens comes up clean and a markdown report is presented, its clean statement for this lens is exactly: `No verification gaps found.`

- Add any newly found unhandled paths to findings; discard confirmed-handled ones

## Step 3: Deletion check

Runs only when the diff removed or replaced meaningful code (ignore pure renames and whitespace). Subordinate to the edge-case pass; findings are usually few or none.

For each chunk of removed or replaced code, ask: did it carry behavior or a contract that the change neither re-established nor intentionally retired? Add a finding for any resulting regression, orphaned reference, or newly-dead code. Skip anything already covered by your edge-case findings. Add nothing if nothing qualifies.

Deletion findings go in the same array with the four standard fields plus:

- `kind`: `"deletion"`
- `confidence`: `"high"`, `"medium"`, or `"low"` — these are inferences; rate them

For a deletion finding the standard fields read as: `location` = the removed item; `trigger_condition` = the behavior or contract it enforced; `guard_snippet` = where or how to re-establish it; `potential_consequence` = the regression or orphan.

## Step 4: Claims check

Runs only when the message that launched you named a claims file. Read that file now, for the first time; the path tracing is finished and the claims cannot steer it retroactively.

The file holds the change's own narrative — commit messages and any stated description. The narrative is the author's testimony, not evidence: a claim repeated in a code comment is still the same claim, not confirmation. Extract each checkable claim — what the change does, what it preserves, ordering, arithmetic, and parity with existing code ("exactly as X does") — then try to falsify each one against the code you have already traced. Where your trace is not enough to decide, read the code that decides it: the compared-to function, the actual callee, the state the claim assumes.

Claim findings go in the same array with the four standard fields plus:

- `kind`: `"claim"`
- `confidence`: `"high"`, `"medium"`, or `"low"`

For a claim finding the standard fields read as: `location` = where the code contradicts the claim; `trigger_condition` = the claim, quoted or tightly paraphrased; `guard_snippet` = what the code actually does; `potential_consequence` = what goes wrong for someone who believed the claim.

Verified claims produce nothing. Add nothing if nothing is falsified.

## Findings shape

Each edge-case finding contains exactly these four fields:

```json
[{
  "location": "file:start-end (or file:line when single line, or file:hunk when exact line unavailable)",
  "trigger_condition": "one-line description (max 15 words)",
  "guard_snippet": "minimal code sketch that closes the gap (single-line escaped string, no raw newlines or unescaped quotes)",
  "potential_consequence": "what could actually go wrong (max 15 words)"
}]
```

An empty array is valid when nothing is found. Do not assign severity labels, rankings, or priority levels.
# Verification-Gap Lens

**Goal:** Find behavior this change altered that could break later without any test failing. Do not hunt for bugs; report the ones you run into while tracing.

A gap finding is a request to add or change one test. File it only when you can name a specific regression that test would catch. If no such test is worth writing, there is nothing to file.

Gap shapes:

1. **Regression gap:** the changed code could regress where it is used, and no test would fail.
2. **Missing-adoption gap:** a site that should use the new behavior still handles the case its own way, and no test would catch that.
3. **Broken-verification gap:** a test looks like it covers the change but does not: it is skipped, flaky, not run normally, or too weak to see the regression.
4. **Stale-verification gap:** a test this change made wrong or moot. It may still pass.

## Evidence rules

- Read a test before saying what it covers or misses.
- Before saying no test exists, search the repo for the symbol under test and its imports. Expected file locations are not enough.
- Say what you checked and how far you looked. Drop any finding you cannot ground.
- Do not assign severity, confidence, priority, or ranking.

## Sequence

### Step 1: Screen

Take each part of the change separately. Skip a part that changes no behavior: no change to return values, thrown errors, side effects callers can see, or observable state (including iteration order and emitted messages). Formatting, comments, renames, trivial getters and pass-throughs, and type-only changes are examples. Once a part is skipped, do not look at its callers or tests.

Also skip parts that are not worth a test: static text such as prompts, skills, and documents; LLM output; and build, toolchain, dependency, and configuration changes that the build or CI run itself checks. Deterministic code that builds a prompt or request, or handles a model's response, is still eligible; the model call itself is not, and existing tests that call a model are not precedent for more.

Do not skip test-only parts. A deleted or weakened test is checked in Step 4; every touched test is read in Step 5.

If every part is skipped, return zero findings (`[]`). When the output format includes a markdown report, note there that the change is non-behavioral; a caller's exact zero-findings output contract wins over this note.

### Step 2: Name the changed behavior

For each remaining part, say what behavior differs from before: output, side effect, branch, error path, schema or event shape, default, validation rule, external contract. Handle each behavior separately.

### Step 3: Find where it is used

Trace each changed behavior to the code that observes it: direct callers, registered entry points (routes, commands, DI), and contract consumers (schemas, events, APIs, database readers).

Stop a path when a test there would catch a regression, when the consumer does not observe the change, or when the next hop is a guess (dynamic dispatch, reflection, code outside the repo). One to three hops is usually enough. With more than five similar consumers, check representative ones and expand only when a consumer uses the behavior differently.

### Step 4: Name the regression, then check the test

For each consumer, name the smallest realistic regression it would see: the branch inverted, the default dropped, the field omitted, the old error code returned, the integration call skipped. This is the Demonstration. It describes what goes wrong for the consumer. "This line could be removed without a test failing" is not a regression. If there is no regression (the state is unreachable, the branch is defensive, the code repeats what another line already guarantees), drop the path. There is no finding and nowhere else to file it.

A missing-adoption gap needs two things: evidence the change means the new behavior to replace the local one (PR intent, naming or docs, a replaced sibling site, deleted duplicate logic, a test defining the new rule), and the same observable contract at both sites. Without both, it is a refactor suggestion, not a finding. With both, missing coverage of the non-adoption is the gap.

Read the relevant test. Would the Demonstration make an assertion fail?

- Yes: the behavior is verified. No finding.
- No test runs the path, or the test is skipped, flaky, or not run normally, or it runs the code without checking the changed result: report a regression gap or broken-verification gap.
- No test asserts the site adopts the new behavior: report a missing-adoption gap.

A test counts only when it runs normally and an assertion observes the changed output, branch, or contract. These do not count: assertions on source text; success, no-throw, or snapshot-only checks; mock or log-call checks; manual checks; tests that mock away the integration; end-to-end tests that pass through without checking the changed output; stale assertions or fixtures. For example, `expect(x ?? DEFAULT).toBe(DEFAULT)` passes when `x` is missing.

Common patterns: a helper test covers the branch but caller values skip it; a payload or schema change is not checked at the consumer; migration tests only create new-format rows; a handled partial-failure path has no test; a deleted or weakened test leaves behavior unpinned (deleting a source-text assertion is not this).

### Step 5: Check the touched tests

A test is wrong when what it asserts is not what the code should do after this change. A test or test comment is moot when it no longer exercises or describes anything. Report either as a stale-verification gap, saying what the test should assert instead, or that it should go.

### Step 6: Confirm

Before writing a finding, re-open the tests or search results it relies on. Check that the Demonstration names a regression and no test you read would catch it, or that the stale assertion pins the outcome you say it does. Explain why the test misses the regression from what it sets up and checks.

Do not report: cases the compiler or type checker enforces; behavior an integration, contract, or end-to-end test already verifies; low coverage or a missing test file by itself; untested code the change did not touch.

Defects you ran into while tracing are reported with `gap_shape: "other"`. Do not go looking for more.

## Findings shape

Emit each gap with the canonical fields plus this lens's extras:

- `location` — the behavior or contract that changed, `file:line`
- `trigger_condition` — the gap, in one line
- `guard_snippet` — the test to add or change: the assertion or check that is absent, or how the stale assertion should read, fit to how this repo already tests
- `potential_consequence` — the regression, and why the tests you read would not fail; for a missing-adoption gap, the case the site mishandles; for a stale-verification gap, what the code should do, and why the test does not say so
- `gap_shape` — `"regression-gap"`, `"missing-adoption-gap"`, `"broken-verification-gap"`, `"stale-verification-gap"`, or `"other"`
- `consumer` — the impacted consumer or site, named concretely with `file:line`, not "callers of this function"
- `evidence` — what the relevant test asserts, with `file:line`; or the searches run and their result; for a broken-verification gap, why the apparent test does not count; for a stale-verification gap, the assertion that is wrong or moot

For `gap_shape: "other"` findings the four canonical fields suffice (description only); `consumer` and `evidence` are optional. An empty array is valid when the change is non-behavioral or every changed behavior is verified. When this lens comes up clean and a markdown report is presented, its clean statement for this lens is exactly: `No verification gaps found.`

"""Load or reload offices and people from a CSV (R8, AD-9).

    python -m roombooker.seed <file.csv>

Columns: email, name, office, office_manager. People are matched on email; anyone
missing from the file is marked inactive and keeps their id. Offices are created by
name and never deleted. The whole file loads in one transaction, or nothing does.
"""

import argparse
import csv
import logging
import sys
from collections.abc import Sequence
from pathlib import Path

from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from roombooker.core.db import get_engine
from roombooker.people import store

log = logging.getLogger("roombooker.seed")

COLUMNS = ("email", "name", "office", "office_manager")
TRUE_VALUES = {"true", "yes", "1"}
FALSE_VALUES = {"false", "no", "0", ""}


class SeedError(Exception):
    """The file cannot be loaded. Each problem names its line."""

    def __init__(self, problems: list[str]):
        super().__init__("\n".join(problems))
        self.problems = problems


def parse(path: Path) -> list[store.PersonRecord]:
    """Read and validate the whole file. Raises SeedError listing every problem."""
    try:
        handle = path.open(newline="", encoding="utf-8-sig")
    except OSError as exc:
        raise SeedError([f"{path}: cannot open ({exc.strerror})"]) from exc

    with handle:
        reader = csv.DictReader(handle)
        header = [(name or "").strip().lower() for name in reader.fieldnames or []]
        missing = [c for c in COLUMNS if c not in header]
        if missing:
            names = ", ".join(missing)
            raise SeedError([f"line 1: missing column{'s' if len(missing) > 1 else ''} {names}"])
        reader.fieldnames = header

        problems: list[str] = []
        records: list[store.PersonRecord] = []
        first_line_for_email: dict[str, int] = {}
        for row in reader:
            line = reader.line_num
            email = (row.get("email") or "").strip().lower()
            name = (row.get("name") or "").strip()
            office = (row.get("office") or "").strip()
            flag = (row.get("office_manager") or "").strip().lower()

            row_problems = []
            if not email:
                row_problems.append("empty email")
            if not name:
                row_problems.append("empty name")
            if not office:
                row_problems.append("empty office")
            if flag not in TRUE_VALUES | FALSE_VALUES:
                row_problems.append(
                    f"unknown office_manager value {row.get('office_manager', '').strip()!r} "
                    "(use true/yes/1, false/no/0 or leave blank)"
                )
            if email and email in first_line_for_email:
                row_problems.append(
                    f"duplicate email {email} (first on line {first_line_for_email[email]})"
                )
            elif email:
                first_line_for_email[email] = line

            if row_problems:
                problems.extend(f"line {line}: {p}" for p in row_problems)
            else:
                records.append(store.PersonRecord(email, name, office, flag in TRUE_VALUES))

    if problems:
        raise SeedError(problems)
    if not records:
        raise SeedError([f"{path}: no people in the file; refusing to mark everyone inactive"])
    return records


def load(path: Path) -> store.LoadResult:
    """Validate `path`, then load it in one transaction."""
    records = parse(path)
    with Session(get_engine()) as session, session.begin():
        return store.load_people(session, records)


def main(argv: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="python -m roombooker.seed", description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
    parser.add_argument("csv_file", type=Path, help="CSV with columns " + ", ".join(COLUMNS))
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    try:
        result = load(args.csv_file)
    except SeedError as exc:
        log.error("seed: %s not loaded, nothing written", args.csv_file)
        for problem in exc.problems:
            print(f"error: {problem}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    log.info(
        "seed: loaded %s: %d offices (%d new), people %d added, %d updated (%d reactivated), "
        "%d marked inactive",
        args.csv_file,
        result.offices_total,
        result.offices_created,
        result.added,
        result.updated,
        result.reactivated,
        len(result.deactivated_ids),
    )
    for person_id in result.deactivated_ids:
        log.info("seed: marked inactive person_id=%d", person_id)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    logging.basicConfig(
        level=logging.INFO, format="%(levelname)s %(name)s: %(message)s", stream=sys.stdout
    )
    sys.exit(main())

def test_switch_name_returns_to_same_page(page: Page):
    # Neither is an office manager: since story 2, `/` sends office managers to Manage rooms.
    page.goto("/?from=switch")
    pick(page, "fras", "Chloe Fraser")
    expect(page).to_have_url(re.compile(r"/\?from=switch$"))

    page.locator(".top-bar .current-person").click()
    expect(page.get_by_role("heading", name="Pick your name")).to_be_visible()
    pick(page, "kieran", "Kieran Walsh")

    expect(page).to_have_url(re.compile(r"/\?from=switch$"))
    expect(top_bar_name(page)).to_have_text("Kieran Walsh")


def test_reload_without_person_sends_them_to_pick_your_name(page: Page, live_server, tmp_path):
    page.goto("/")
    pick(page, "adeyemi", "Ben Adeyemi")
    expect(top_bar_name(page)).to_have_text("Ben Adeyemi")
    before = live_server.person_ids()

    lines = BUILD_SEED.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
    without_ben = tmp_path / "without-ben.csv"
    without_ben.write_text(
        "\n".join(line for line in lines if not line.startswith("ben.adeyemi@")) + "\n",
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    live_server.seed(without_ben)

    page.reload()
    expect(page).to_have_url(re.compile(r"/pick-name\?next=/$"))
    page.get_by_label("Your name").fill("adeyemi")
    expect(page.get_by_text("No one called “adeyemi”.")).to_be_visible()

    after = live_server.person_ids()
    assert {e: i for e, (i, _) in after.items()} == {e: i for e, (i, _) in before.items()}
    assert after["ben.adeyemi@example.com"][1] == 0

echo "--- R3-R5 add/edit/close/reopen (no-JS)"

echo -n "edit -> Boardroom 10       : "; st -b person_id=$ANNA -X POST -d 'name=Boardroom&capacity=10' $B/manage-rooms/$RID
echo -n "close                      : "; st -b person_id=$ANNA -X POST $B/manage-rooms/$RID/close
echo -n "status after close         : "; curl -s -b person_id=$ANNA $B/manage-rooms | grep -o '<td class="room-status">[A-Za-z]*' | head -1
echo -n "reopen                     : "; st -b person_id=$ANNA -X POST $B/manage-rooms/$RID/reopen
echo -n "db row                     : "; sqlite3 "$ROOMBOOKER_DB_PATH" "select name,capacity,is_closed from rooms where id=$RID"
echo "--- R7 invalid"
echo -n "capacity 0                 : "; st -b person_id=$ANNA -X POST -d 'name=X&capacity=0' $B/manage-rooms
echo -n "duplicate (case)           : "; curl -s -b person_id=$ANNA -X POST -d 'name=BOARDROOM&capacity=3' $B/manage-rooms | grep -o 'already has a room called [^<]*'
echo "--- R6 refusals"
echo -n "Hannah GET /manage-rooms   : "; st -b person_id=$HANNAH $B/manage-rooms
echo -n "Joanne POST close London   : "; st -b person_id=$JOANNE -X POST $B/manage-rooms/$RID/close
echo "--- Cross-story: stale cookie on a POST-only route (identity from 1.1, routes from 1.2)"
for P in "/manage-rooms/$RID" "/manage-rooms/$RID/reopen"; do
  echo -n "POST $P junk cookie       : "; LOC=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{redirect_url}' -b person_id=999999 -X POST -d 'name=A&capacity=2' $B$P); echo "$LOC"
  NEXT=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{redirect_url}' -X POST -d "person_id=$ANNA&next=${P}" $B/pick-name)

done
echo -n "htmx POST reopen junk cookie HX-Redirect: "; curl -s -D - -o /dev/null -H 'HX-Request: true' -b person_id=999999 -X POST $B/manage-rooms/$RID/reopen | grep -i hx-redirect
echo "--- RULE-6 log lines"
grep -E "rooms: person_id|pick: person_id" "$WORK/server.log" | head -8

row.get_by_role("button", name=re.compile("^Reopen")).click()
    expect(page).to_have_url(re.compile(r"/manage-rooms\?notice=reopened&room=\d+$"))
    expect(announce).to_have_text(f"Reopened {renamed}.")
    expect(row.locator(".room-status")).to_have_text("Open")


def test_office_manager_of_another_office_is_refused(page: Page, live_server):
    name = unique("Boardroom")
    room_id = add_london_room(live_server, name)

    page.goto("/")
    pick(page, "price", "Joanne Price")
    expect(page).to_have_url(re.compile(r"/manage-rooms$"))
    expect(page.locator(".page .meta")).to_have_text("Manchester")
    expect(page.get_by_text(name, exact=True)).to_have_count(0)

    page.goto(f"/manage-rooms/{room_id}/close")  # the direct link
    expect(page.locator("#announce")).to_have_text(REFUSED)

    response = page.request.post(f"/manage-rooms/{room_id}/close")  # the direct request
    assert response.status == 403
    assert REFUSED in response.text()
    assert room_in_db(live_server, name) == (room_id, 0)

# Retrospective — epic-offices-and-rooms

## Epic summary

- Epic: `epic-offices-and-rooms`, "Office managers keep their rooms current" (`epic-offices-and-rooms.md`, `status: done`, closed in `696ebff`).
- Tickets, in build order: 1.1 Pick and switch your name, end to end (`done`); 1.2 Office managers manage their office's rooms (`done`).
- `pending_tickets`: none. Tickets at `built`: none.
- Going-in concerns from the user: none.

### Plan ranges

| Ticket | Plan | baseline_revision | Range | Commits |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1.1 | `tickets/story-pick-and-switch-your-name-end-to-end-plan.md` | `8a7db0e` | `8a7db0e..22bbc6a` (recorded) | `cf77262` feat, `22bbc6a` mark done |
| 1.2 | `tickets/story-office-managers-manage-their-office-s-rooms-plan.md` | `22bbc6a` | `22bbc6a..696ebff` (HEAD, inferred) | `d2a5b1f` feat, `b28a00b` mark done, `696ebff` epic close (planning files only) |

Neither range has merges (`merge_count` 0). None of the epic's code is on `main`. `main` is still at `8a7db0e`, and the work sits on stacked branches, `story-1-1-pick-your-name` then `story-1-2-manage-rooms` (`git log --decorate`).

### Evidence inventory

| Evidence | Status |
|---|---|
| Epic file: Requirements R1–R9 and Done when | Read in full. Criteria are **declared**. |
| Ticket entries (`tickets.toml`, `find 1.1`, `find 1.2`) | Read. Both carry a description and a verify step; neither was pulled. |
| Story files | None. Neither ticket was pulled (`story_file: null`), so the entries are the spec. |
| Plans | Both read in full: frozen intent, Code Map, Implementation Notes, Review Triage Log, Design Notes, Verification. |
| Dated `## Code Review` blocks | Absent from both plans. Review is recorded in the Review Triage Log: quick lens only, `review_source: pinned`. |
| Plan Change Log | Present and empty in both plans. |
| `git_evidence.py` | Run once per range. |
| Run folders (`<type>-*/`) | None in the epic folder. |
| Companions | Architecture spine opened for AD-1 (with its diagram) and AD-12 only. |
| Epic `.memlog.md` | Read. |
| Previous retrospective | None. This is the first epic in `epics` order. |
| Session logs | Found in `~/.claude/projects/-home-claude-runs-room-booker/`: `79383f16` (build 1.1), `6fb5ad90` (mark 1.1 done), `cad2024f` (build 1.2), `30bc71ce` (mark 1.2 done), `4c3fae67` (epic close). Main-thread messages read. The build subagent transcripts were not inspected. |

## Findings

Each ID is cited in Action items. Each disposition gives what to do about this instance, then what would prevent the next one.

### Behavior and spec reconciliation

**F1. A stale cookie on a POST-only route ends on a JSON 405 page after re-picking (R2).** Story 1.1's `NeedsPerson` sets `next` to the request path for every method (`roombooker/core/identity.py:63`). Story 1.2 then added POST-only routes: `POST /manage-rooms/{id}` and `POST /manage-rooms/{id}/reopen` (`roombooker/rooms/web.py:157,220`). When the cookie is missing, unknown or inactive at the moment of a write, the person goes to `/pick-name?next=/manage-rooms/1/reopen`. After they pick, the browser GETs that path and receives `405 {"detail":"Method Not Allowed"}`. The behavior check below reproduced this for both routes, and for htmx, which gets `HX-Redirect=/pick-name?next=/manage-rooms/1/reopen`. R2 promises a return "to the page asked for". This is a seam no single session saw: the 1.1 review never saw POST routes, and the 1.2 review never revisited the identity redirect. Sources: bmad-review adversarial, edge-case and verification-gap lenses; behavior check.
- Disposition: **fix now** (small; see A1).
- Prevent: when a story adds routes behind `CurrentPerson`, its verify step includes the stale-cookie round trip.

**F2. The framework's 404, 405 and 422 responses are JSON.** `roombooker/app.py:41-42` registers handlers only for `NeedsPerson` and `DomainError`. Starlette's HTTP errors and `RequestValidationError` fall through to FastAPI's JSON defaults, as F1 shows. Story 1.1 already patched one instance by hand (plan 1, Review Triage #4: "`gone=x` returns a JSON 422"), so this has now come up in both stories. It conflicts with plan 1's "Never: a JSON API" and with AD-12's one error path. Source: adversarial lens; plan 1 Review Triage Log #4.
- Disposition: **fix now** together with F1 (A1).
- Prevent: add a core rule that every response is HTML (see A5).

**F3. The 1.1 switch behavior changed under `/manage-rooms`.** From Manage rooms, the switch link now goes through `/` (`roombooker/templates/base.html:22`), not back to the same page as 1.1's AC2 said. Story 1.2's review made this change deliberately (plan 2, Review Triage #1) so that switching to someone who doesn't manage that office doesn't land on a 403. It is tested at `tests/test_rooms.py:97`.
- Disposition: **accept**. This is a recorded deviation, so later retros should not flag it again.
- Prevent: nothing.

**F4. Known issue: an htmx add discards a row open for Edit or close confirmation.** See `roombooker/rooms/web.py:132-143`. Plan 2 Review Triage #3 rejected it as unlikely, and the epic Notes list it as "Known issue, not ticketed".
- Disposition: **defer**. The epic Notes carry enough context to pick it up later (A6).
- Prevent: nothing.

Everything else checked out. The epic file's R1, R3–R9, its constraints (RULE-4, RULE-6 logging, RULE-9 widths) and each Done when line match the as-built code, and the behavior check and test suite confirm it. R7's limits (50 characters; capacity 1–200) match `roombooker/rooms/service.py:21-23`, after the epic file was reconciled in `696ebff`.

### Architecture delta

The import graph was derived from `roombooker/**` imports with an inline grep; no dependency tool was run.

**F5. `core` depends upward on `people.service`, against the spine's diagram.** The AD-1 diagram shows `core` "used by all" and says dependencies "never point upward or in a cycle". In the code:
- `roombooker/core/identity.py:17-18` imports `people.service`.
- `roombooker/core/errors.py:32-33` lazily imports `core.identity`, so `rooms.service → core.errors → core.identity → people.service`.
- `roombooker/people/service.py:3` guards the cycle by convention only: "Must never import `core.identity`".

Plan 1's Code Map chose this on purpose ("`identity.py` imports `people.service`"), but the spine was never updated to match.
- Disposition: **accept** the structure, and **reconcile the spine**: state that `core.identity` sits above `people.service` (A4).
- Prevent: a plan that departs from a spine diagram should record a spine change in its Plan Change Log.

**F6. `_person_for_top_bar` runs its own session outside dependency injection.** It drives `get_session()` by hand and re-runs `current_person` in a second session, which bypasses FastAPI dependency overrides and adds a second lookup per refusal (`roombooker/core/errors.py:26-41`). Source: adversarial lens.
- Disposition: **defer**, folded into the core refactor (A2).

No layering violations between stores: each store is imported only by its own service, plus `people.store` by the seed CLI.

### Duplication map

**F7. Request helpers are re-solved in each web module.**
- The `HX-Request` check appears four times: `core/identity.py:96`, `core/errors.py:46`, `people/web.py:47` and `rooms/web.py:34`.
- `_render` appears twice and the copies differ: `people/web.py:21` doesn't set `Vary`, while `rooms/web.py:38` does.
- The `DbSession` alias is defined twice: `people/web.py:18` and `rooms/web.py:22`.

`bookings.web` and `calendar.web` are next, and each will copy one of these. Source: adversarial lens.
- Disposition: **defer** to a small refactor before epic-find-and-book's first web story (A2).
- Prevent: the epic declined a refactor sweep (epic Notes, "no refactor sweep … since the epic has two entries"). This finding is what such a sweep would have caught.

**F8. Two conventions guard against SQLite integer overflow on ids.** `core/identity.py:60` and `people/web.py:63` accept at most 18 digits, which also refuses valid 19-digit ids. `rooms/service.py:83` bounds by value, `<= 2**63-1`.
- Disposition: **defer** into A2, as one `parse_id` in core.

### Pattern divergence

**F9. `NotAllowed` in core has a rooms-specific default message.** `roombooker/core/errors.py:21-23` defaults to "Only office managers can manage rooms.". epic-find-and-book will raise `NotAllowed` for RULE-3 and show that wording unless every raise passes its own message.
- Disposition: **fix in A2**, before epic-find-and-book raises it.

**F10. The `rooms` query table leaves out its foreign key.** `roombooker/rooms/store.py:19` has no ForeignKey (only a comment), while `people/store.py:40` declares one.
- Disposition: **accept**. It is cosmetic, because the migration enforces the key.

### God-class and size growth

Checked, and clean. The largest Python files are `rooms/web.py` (224 lines) and `rooms/service.py` (210). `static/app.css` reached 508 lines over the two stories (+245, +263). It is still a single stylesheet; watch it as find-and-book and calendar add screens. No `binary_revisions`, and no merges went unmeasured.

### Diff-scope review (bmad-review: adversarial, edge-case, verification-gap)

The review ran over `8a7db0e..696ebff` for code only (excluding `_bmad-output/`, `uv.lock` and the vendored htmx), weighting the seams between the two stories. The three lenses ran **inline, one after another, not as parallel subagents**. That narrows the review: one reviewer played each lens, so independent disagreement between lenses was lost. Raw findings: `/tmp/claude-0/-home-claude-runs-room-booker/9e7dff7d-2e77-46a5-aab9-4e990d3104df/scratchpad/epic-review-findings.json` (17 entries). They are already folded into F1, F2 and F5–F10 above. The ones not covered there:

- **F11.** The seed matches office names case-sensitively (`roombooker/seed.py:60`, `people/store.py:98-105`). An HR file that says "london" would create a fourth office and move people and their manager rights away from London's rooms. Disposition: **defer to epic-deployment**, which owns loading HR's list (A7).
- **F12.** The case-insensitive room-name rule lives only in Python, while the database constraint is exact-match (`rooms/service.py:89-97`, `0002_rooms.py:33`), so two concurrent adds with different case could both commit. Disposition: **accept**. Plan 2's Design Notes chose this, and one office manager per office makes concurrency negligible.
- **F13.** htmx `responseHandling` swaps only 2xx, 403, 404 and 422 (`base.html:6`). A 400, 405 or 500 during an htmx Save or Close shows nothing. Disposition: **fix with A1**.
- **F14.** A name made only of zero-width or control characters passes the non-empty check (`rooms/service.py:107-111`). Disposition: **accept**. It is low-value.

## Findings

Each ID is cited in Action items. Each disposition gives what to do about this instance, then what would prevent the next one.

### Behavior and spec reconciliation

**F1. A stale cookie on a POST-only route ends on a JSON 405 page after re-picking (R2).** Story 1.1's `NeedsPerson` sets `next` to the request path for every method (`roombooker/core/identity.py:63`). Story 1.2 then added POST-only routes: `POST /manage-rooms/{id}` and `POST /manage-rooms/{id}/reopen` (`roombooker/rooms/web.py:157,220`). When the cookie is missing, unknown or inactive at the moment of a write, the person goes to `/pick-name?next=/manage-rooms/1/reopen`. After they pick, the browser GETs that path and receives `405 {"detail":"Method Not Allowed"}`. The behavior check below reproduced this for both routes, and for htmx, which gets `HX-Redirect=/pick-name?next=/manage-rooms/1/reopen`. R2 promises a return "to the page asked for". This is a seam no single session saw: the 1.1 review never saw POST routes, and the 1.2 review never revisited the identity redirect. Sources: bmad-review adversarial, edge-case and verification-gap lenses; behavior check.
- Disposition: **fix now** (small; see A1).
- Prevent: when a story adds routes behind `CurrentPerson`, its verify step includes the stale-cookie round trip.

**F2. The framework's 404, 405 and 422 responses are JSON.** `roombooker/app.py:41-42` registers handlers only for `NeedsPerson` and `DomainError`. Starlette's HTTP errors and `RequestValidationError` fall through to FastAPI's JSON defaults, as F1 shows. Story 1.1 already patched one instance by hand (plan 1, Review Triage #4: "`gone=x` returns a JSON 422"), so this has now come up in both stories. It conflicts with plan 1's "Never: a JSON API" and with AD-12's one error path. Source: adversarial lens; plan 1 Review Triage Log #4.
- Disposition: **fix now** together with F1 (A1).
- Prevent: add a core rule that every response is HTML (see A5).

**F3. The 1.1 switch behavior changed under `/manage-rooms`.** From Manage rooms, the switch link now goes through `/` (`roombooker/templates/base.html:22`), not back to the same page as 1.1's AC2 said. Story 1.2's review made this change deliberately (plan 2, Review Triage #1) so that switching to someone who doesn't manage that office doesn't land on a 403. It is tested at `tests/test_rooms.py:97`.
- Disposition: **accept**. This is a recorded deviation, so later retros should not flag it again.
- Prevent: nothing.

**F4. Known issue: an htmx add discards a row open for Edit or close confirmation.** See `roombooker/rooms/web.py:132-143`. Plan 2 Review Triage #3 rejected it as unlikely, and the epic Notes list it as "Known issue, not ticketed".
- Disposition: **defer**. The epic Notes carry enough context to pick it up later (A6).
- Prevent: nothing.

Everything else checked out. The epic file's R1, R3–R9, its constraints (RULE-4, RULE-6 logging, RULE-9 widths) and each Done when line match the as-built code, and the behavior check and test suite confirm it. R7's limits (50 characters; capacity 1–200) match `roombooker/rooms/service.py:21-23`, after the epic file was reconciled in `696ebff`.

### Architecture delta

The import graph was derived from `roombooker/**` imports with an inline grep; no dependency tool was run.

**F5. `core` depends upward on `people.service`, against the spine's diagram.** The AD-1 diagram shows `core` "used by all" and says dependencies "never point upward or in a cycle". In the code:
- `roombooker/core/identity.py:17-18` imports `people.service`.
- `roombooker/core/errors.py:32-33` lazily imports `core.identity`, so `rooms.service → core.errors → core.identity → people.service`.
- `roombooker/people/service.py:3` guards the cycle by convention only: "Must never import `core.identity`".

Plan 1's Code Map chose this on purpose ("`identity.py` imports `people.service`"), but the spine was never updated to match.
- Disposition: **accept** the structure, and **reconcile the spine**: state that `core.identity` sits above `people.service` (A4).
- Prevent: a plan that departs from a spine diagram should record a spine change in its Plan Change Log.

**F6. `_person_for_top_bar` runs its own session outside dependency injection.** It drives `get_session()` by hand and re-runs `current_person` in a second session, which bypasses FastAPI dependency overrides and adds a second lookup per refusal (`roombooker/core/errors.py:26-41`). Source: adversarial lens.
- Disposition: **defer**, folded into the core refactor (A2).

No layering violations between stores: each store is imported only by its own service, plus `people.store` by the seed CLI.

### Duplication map

**F7. Request helpers are re-solved in each web module.**
- The `HX-Request` check appears four times: `core/identity.py:96`, `core/errors.py:46`, `people/web.py:47` and `rooms/web.py:34`.
- `_render` appears twice and the copies differ: `people/web.py:21` doesn't set `Vary`, while `rooms/web.py:38` does.
- The `DbSession` alias is defined twice: `people/web.py:18` and `rooms/web.py:22`.

`bookings.web` and `calendar.web` are next, and each will copy one of these. Source: adversarial lens.
- Disposition: **defer** to a small refactor before epic-find-and-book's first web story (A2).
- Prevent: the epic declined a refactor sweep (epic Notes, "no refactor sweep … since the epic has two entries"). This finding is what such a sweep would have caught.

**F8. Two conventions guard against SQLite integer overflow on ids.** `core/identity.py:60` and `people/web.py:63` accept at most 18 digits, which also refuses valid 19-digit ids. `rooms/service.py:83` bounds by value, `<= 2**63-1`.
- Disposition: **defer** into A2, as one `parse_id` in core.

### Pattern divergence

**F9. `NotAllowed` in core has a rooms-specific default message.** `roombooker/core/errors.py:21-23` defaults to "Only office managers can manage rooms.". epic-find-and-book will raise `NotAllowed` for RULE-3 and show that wording unless every raise passes its own message.
- Disposition: **fix in A2**, before epic-find-and-book raises it.

**F10. The `rooms` query table leaves out its foreign key.** `roombooker/rooms/store.py:19` has no ForeignKey (only a comment), while `people/store.py:40` declares one.
- Disposition: **accept**. It is cosmetic, because the migration enforces the key.

### God-class and size growth

Checked, and clean. The largest Python files are `rooms/web.py` (224 lines) and `rooms/service.py` (210). `static/app.css` reached 508 lines over the two stories (+245, +263). It is still a single stylesheet; watch it as find-and-book and calendar add screens. No `binary_revisions`, and no merges went unmeasured.

### Diff-scope review (bmad-review: adversarial, edge-case, verification-gap)

The review ran over `8a7db0e..696ebff` for code only (excluding `_bmad-output/`, `uv.lock` and the vendored htmx), weighting the seams between the two stories. The three lenses ran **inline, one after another, not as parallel subagents**. That narrows the review: one reviewer played each lens, so independent disagreement between lenses was lost. Raw findings: `/tmp/claude-0/-home-claude-runs-room-booker/9e7dff7d-2e77-46a5-aab9-4e990d3104df/scratchpad/epic-review-findings.json` (17 entries). They are already folded into F1, F2 and F5–F10 above. The ones not covered there:

- **F11.** The seed matches office names case-sensitively (`roombooker/seed.py:60`, `people/store.py:98-105`). An HR file that says "london" would create a fourth office and move people and their manager rights away from London's rooms. Disposition: **defer to epic-deployment**, which owns loading HR's list (A7).
- **F12.** The case-insensitive room-name rule lives only in Python, while the database constraint is exact-match (`rooms/service.py:89-97`, `0002_rooms.py:33`), so two concurrent adds with different case could both commit. Disposition: **accept**. Plan 2's Design Notes chose this, and one office manager per office makes concurrency negligible.
- **F13.** htmx `responseHandling` swaps only 2xx, 403, 404 and 422 (`base.html:6`). A 400, 405 or 500 during an htmx Save or Close shows nothing. Disposition: **fix with A1**.
- **F14.** A name made only of zero-width or control characters passes the non-empty check (`rooms/service.py:107-111`). Disposition: **accept**. It is low-value.
- **F15 (verification gap).** Nothing asserts that the 403 page keeps the current name and Switch link (`core/errors.py:61`). The tests check only `#announce` and the absence of tabs (`tests/test_rooms.py:276-280`, `tests/e2e/test_manage_rooms.py:176-181`). Disposition: **fix with A1**, as one assertion.
- **F16 (verification gap).** No test follows `next` after a non-GET guarded request (`tests/test_people_web.py:114-123` is GET-only). This is the test for F1 (A1).

Claims check: the commit claims that the `person_id` cookie is read only by `core.current_person` (`cf77262`) holds; `request.cookies` appears only at `core/identity.py:58`. The claim of "the AD-12 error handler" (`d2a5b1f`) holds for domain errors only, which is F2.

### Process lessons (session logs and plans)

- **P1. Both plans ran over the 1,600-token plan target:** about 2,370 tokens (`79383f16`, message 138) and about 2,900 (`cad2024f`, message 154). The user chose to keep each one whole. Story 1.2's build went through anyway, with three review patches and no loopback, so the epic Notes' fallback split wasn't needed. Lesson: none required. The target flagged the right story, and the check worked as intended.
- **P2. Nothing was merged to `main`.** The 1.2 session found story 1 unmerged and recommended stacking a branch (`cad2024f`, message 95). The epic then closed with all of its code off `main`. epic-deployment depends on "the app running locally" (`tickets.toml` `after`) and will want a stable base. Lesson: closing an epic should include merging its branches, or recording why not (A3).
- **P3. Each story had only the quick review lens** (`lenses_ran: [quick]`, `review_source: pinned`). It caught real bugs in each story: the 500 on an oversized id, the accented-name search, and the switch-to-403. But no lens looks across stories, which is how F1 got through. Lesson: for a medium-risk story that builds on an earlier story's core, add a check of how the two fit together to its verify step, or keep this retro's cross-story pass as the gate (A5).

I ran the real app factory on a scratch database (Alembic to head, build seed loaded) through `TestClient`, with a script at `/tmp/claude-0/-home-claude-runs-room-booker/9e7dff7d-2e77-46a5-aab9-4e990d3104df/scratchpad/behavior_check.py`. - R6: Hannah on `/manage-rooms` and Joanne closing a London room each get 403, and the room stays open.
- RULE-6: log lines name `person_id` for each pick, add, edit, close, reopen and refusal.
- Where the stories meet: **F1 reproduced.** Re-picking after a stale-cookie POST to `/manage-rooms/1` or `/manage-rooms/1/reopen` ends on a JSON 405. `/close` happens to work because it has a GET confirmation route.
- Suite: `uv run pytest`: **80 passed** (e2e at 1280 and 390 widths, Chromium), with 2 deprecation warnings (httpx in TestClient; a session-scoped fixture written as an instance method).

I didn't visually check the phone layout myself. The epic Notes record that the user walked both stories at both widths.

## Previous-retro follow-through

Nothing to follow through: there is no previous retrospective file. This is the first epic in `epics` order.

## Action items

All of these are proposed. Code fixes go through the normal dev loop (`bmad-build`), and ticket or spine edits through Sofia (`bmad-agent-po`) or Winston (`bmad-agent-architect`).

| # | Action | Findings | Owner | Kind |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | Bug ticket: (a) `NeedsPerson` uses the GET page (`HX-Current-URL`, else `/`) for non-GET requests; (b) HTML handlers for Starlette HTTP errors and `RequestValidationError`; (c) an htmx catch-all so 400, 405 and 500 errors show in `#announce`; (d) tests: follow `next` after a stale-cookie POST to `/manage-rooms/{id}/reopen` and expect a 200 HTML page, and assert the name in the 403 page's top bar. | F1, F2, F13, F15, F16 | Sofia files it; Amelia builds it | remediation |
| A2 | Small refactor story before epic-find-and-book's first web story: move `is_htmx`, `render` (always with `Vary`), `DbSession` and `parse_id` into a core module; give `NotAllowed` a neutral default and move the rooms wording to `rooms.service`; have `current_person` store the `Person` on `request.state` so the error handler stops opening a second session. | F6, F7, F8, F9 | Sofia (ticket in epic-find-and-book); Amelia | remediation |
| A3 | Merge `story-1-2-manage-rooms` into `main` (it includes 1.1), or record why it stays off `main`, before epic-deployment starts. | P2 | User | process |

# Case-insensitive name matching happens in Python, not SQLite

Names the app compares without regard to case (people search on Pick your name, and the rule that room names are unique within an office) are matched with Python's `str.casefold()` over the rows read from the database, not with SQLite's `lower()` or `COLLATE NOCASE`, because SQLite folds only ASCII: in story 1.1's review, `lower('Ó Briain')` returned `'Ó briain'`, so a search typed in another case missed accented names that HR's real list will contain (plan `story-pick-and-switch-your-name-end-to-end-plan.md`, Review Triage Log #3; commit `cf77262`). Story 1.2 applied the same rule to room names: the service trims and casefolds to detect a duplicate, and the database keeps the exact-match unique constraint `uq_rooms_office_id_name` only as a backstop, with an `IntegrityError` mapped to the same refusal (plan `story-office-managers-manage-their-office-s-rooms-plan.md`, Design Notes; commit `d2a5b1f`). The trade-off is that matching reads every active person or every room in the office into Python, which the plans judged cheap at a few hundred rows, and that the database alone does not enforce case-insensitive uniqueness, so two concurrent adds differing only in case could both commit; neither plan states a reason for not adding a casefolded column with a unique index instead.
